metaTitle: DzwoniLek — peace of mind, ordinary phone

hero.eyebrow: A voice assistant that remembers the meds
hero.lead: DzwoniLek calls your mom, dad, grandma or grandpa exactly when it's time for their medication. It asks whether they took it, and you see the answer in the app. No smartphone and nothing to install on their side.
hero.screenshotAlt: DzwoniLek dashboard with the list of care recipients, upcoming calls and today's summary
hero.incomingText: Good morning, Halina. Have you taken your morning Acard yet?

why.statement: Most reminder apps assume an older person owns a smartphone, installs an app, remembers a password and never misses a notification. But all it really takes is a phone call.

phone.title: An ordinary phone is enough
phone.text: A landline or a mobile with buttons. If it rings, it works.

noSetup.title: No installs, no passwords
noSetup.text: There is nothing to set up on your loved one's side. You configure everything.

voice.title: A conversation, not a screen
voice.text: A short, kind question about a specific medication. A simple "yes" or "no" is all it takes.

how.title: Five simple steps to peace of mind
how.lead: You set everything up once, in a few minutes. From then on DzwoniLek works every day, on schedule.

ward.title: Add your loved one
ward.text: Enter their name and phone number. That's all we need to call your mom, dad or grandpa.
ward.alt: Add care recipient dialog with name, phone number and SMS notification settings

routine.title: Build a medication routine
routine.text: Pick a time, add medications from the catalog and set the amount, e.g. one tablet or a half. Morning, noon, evening: as many routines as needed.
routine.alt: Routine wizard with Acard and Amlor selected along with their amounts

schedule.title: Approve it, we handle the rest
schedule.text: Approved routines turn into a call schedule on their own. You always see when the next call is due.
schedule.alt: List of approved routines and upcoming calls for a care recipient

call.title: DzwoniLek calls on time
call.text: The voice assistant asks about each medication in turn and understands the answer. Nobody picked up? We'll try again.
call.alt: Call breakdown: the assistant's questions about medications and the recognized answers

result.title: You simply know
result.text: The calendar shows every day and every routine: taken, missed or unanswered. No more calling to ask "Mom, did you take them yet?".
result.alt: Weekly medication calendar marking taken and missed doses

call.title: It sounds like care, not a robot
call.lead: Short, clear and calm. The assistant asks about a specific medication and dose, and understands "yes, just now" as well as a plain "yes".

points.retry: No answer? Another attempt fifteen minutes later.
points.transcript: Every call saved with a transcript and a summary.
points.sms: If a medication wasn't taken, you get a text message.

lines.greeting: Good evening, Halina. This is DzwoniLek, calling about your evening medication.
lines.askFirst: Have you taken Glucophage 850 mg today, one tablet?
lines.askSecond: Great. And Magne B6, also one tablet?
lines.answerSecond: Yes, together with the other one.
lines.goodbye: Thank you. Have a peaceful evening!

medications.title: Know what they take. And what to watch for.
medications.lead: Drug data comes from openFDA, the official database of the U.S. Food and Drug Administration. AI turns long, technical leaflets into a short, plain-language summary: what actually matters to a caregiver.

pipeline.label: How a medication summary is made

summary.title: Summary
summary.text: Short, clear and in your language

medications.aiAlt: AI summary of Acard: what it is, how to take it, when to take it and key warnings
medications.fdaAlt: Original medication documentation from the openFDA database
medications.listAlt: List of all medications taken by the care recipient, with doses and times
medications.listCaption: All of your loved one's medications in one place, with dose and time.
medications.disclaimer: Summaries are for information only and do not replace advice from a doctor or pharmacist.

peace.title: Peace of mind you can see on a calendar
peace.lead: One glance is enough to know everything is fine. And if it isn't, you'll find out right away.

history.title: Week-by-week history
history.text: Every routine and every day in a single view.

alerts.title: A text when something's wrong
alerts.text: You decide: always, only on problems, or never.

peace.calendarAlt: Medication calendar with call results from the last week
peace.callsAlt: Call history with the medication result for every call

sms.label: Text from DzwoniLek
sms.text: Halina Kowalska: evening medication (20:00) not taken. Worth giving her a call.

cta.title: Give yourself peace of mind
cta.lead: Create an account, add your loved one and build the first routine. The first call can ring as soon as today.

footer.tagline: A voice assistant that reminds about medication.
